units.title: K-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

topics.title: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

outcomes.text: Test how stronger or differently directed pushes and pulls change how an object moves.
Use test data to judge whether a design changes an object's speed or direction with a push or pull.
Observe how sunlight warms sand, soil, rocks and water.
Build a structure that reduces how much sunlight warms a spot.

units.title: K-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Use observations to describe what plants and animals, including people, need to live.
Share observations of local weather to describe how it follows patterns over time.
Argue with evidence that plants and animals can change their surroundings to meet needs.
Use a model to show how what living things need relates to where they live.
Ask questions to learn why forecasting helps people prepare for severe weather.
Share ideas for reducing how people harm land, water, air and living things nearby.

units.title: 1-PS4 Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

topics.title: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

outcomes.text: Investigate to show that vibrating things make sound and sound makes things vibrate.
Observe to show that objects can only be seen when light shines on them.
Investigate what happens when different materials block or pass a light beam.
Build a device using light or sound to send a message over a distance.

units.title: 1-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants or animals use their body parts.
Use texts and media to find parent and baby behaviors that help babies survive.

units.title: 1-LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

topics.title: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

outcomes.text: Observe to show that young plants and animals are like, but not identical to, their parents.
Use observations of sun, moon and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
Observe at different times of year to relate hours of daylight to the season.
Investigate to describe and sort materials by properties you can observe.
Analyze test data to pick materials best suited to a purpose.
Observe how an object made of a few pieces can be taken apart and rebuilt into something new.
Argue with evidence that some changes from heating or cooling can be reversed and others cannot.
Investigate whether plants need sunlight and water to grow.
Make a simple model of how an animal spreads seeds or pollinates plants.
Observe plants and animals to compare how much life varies in different habitats.
Use several sources to show that Earth events can happen quickly or slowly.
Compare different solutions that slow or stop wind or water from reshaping land.
Make a model showing the shapes and kinds of land and water in an area.
Gather information on where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.
Ask questions, observe and gather information to define a simple problem solvable with a new or better tool.
Sketch or model how an object's shape helps it do its job.
Analyze test data from two designs for the same problem to compare strengths and weaknesses.

units.title: 3-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

topics.title: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

outcomes.text: Investigate how balanced and unbalanced forces affect an object's motion.
Observe or measure motion to show that a pattern can predict future motion.
Ask questions about cause and effect in electric or magnetic forces between objects not touching.
Define a simple design problem that magnets can help solve.

units.title: 3-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Model that all organisms have different life cycles but share birth, growth, reproduction and death.
Argue that some animals form groups that help members survive.

units.title: 3-LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

topics.title: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

outcomes.text: Analyze data showing traits are inherited from parents and vary within a group.
Use evidence to explain that the environment can influence traits.
Analyze fossil data to learn about organisms and environments of long ago.
Explain how differences among individuals of a species can help in surviving, finding mates and reproducing.
Argue with evidence that in one habitat some organisms thrive, some struggle and some cannot survive.
Judge the merit of a solution to a problem caused by a changing environment and shifting species.
Show typical seasonal weather using data in tables and graphs.
Combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
Judge how well a design reduces the impact of a weather-related hazard.
Use evidence to explain how an object's speed relates to its energy.
Observe that energy moves from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric current.
Ask questions and predict energy changes when objects collide.
Design, test and improve a device that changes energy from one form to another.

units.title: 4-PS4 Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

topics.title: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

outcomes.text: Model waves by amplitude and wavelength and show that waves can move objects.
Model how light bouncing off objects and entering the eye lets us see them.
Create and compare solutions that use patterns to send information.

units.title: 4-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Argue that internal and external body structures help survival, growth, behavior and reproduction.
Model how animals take in information with senses, process it in the brain and respond.
Use rock layers and fossils as evidence for how a landscape has changed.
Gather evidence of weathering and the rate of erosion from water, ice, wind or plants.
Read map data to describe patterns in Earth's features.
Combine information showing energy and fuels come from natural resources and affect the environment.
Create and compare solutions that reduce harm to people from natural Earth processes.
Model that matter is made of particles too small to see.
Measure and graph to show total weight stays the same through heating, cooling or mixing.
Use observations and measurements to identify materials by their properties.
Investigate whether mixing substances makes new substances.

units.title: 5-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

topics.title: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

outcomes.text: Argue that Earth's gravity pulls objects downward.
Model that the energy in food was once energy from the sun.

units.title: 5-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Argue that plants get materials for growth mainly from air and water.
Model how matter moves among plants, animals, decomposers and the environment.
Argue that the sun looks brighter than other stars because it is closer.
Graph shadow changes, day and night, and seasonal stars to show sky patterns.
Model an example of how the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere or atmosphere interact.
Graph amounts of salt and fresh water in reservoirs to show how Earth's water is distributed.
Gather information on how communities use science to protect resources and the environment.
Define a design problem with success criteria and limits on materials, time or cost.
Generate and compare solutions by how well they meet the criteria and constraints.
Run fair tests with controlled variables to find what in a model needs improving.
Model the atoms that make up simple molecules and extended structures.
Analyze data on substances before and after they interact to tell whether a reaction happened.
Describe how synthetic materials come from natural resources and affect society.
Model how particle motion, temperature and state change when heat is added or removed.
Model that atoms are not created or destroyed in a reaction, so mass is conserved.
Design, test and modify a device that releases or absorbs heat through a chemical reaction.

units.title: MS-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

topics.title: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

outcomes.text: Apply Newton's third law to design a solution for two colliding objects.
Plan an investigation showing motion change depends on the net force and the object's mass.
Ask questions about data to find what affects the strength of electric and magnetic forces.
Argue with evidence that gravity is attractive and depends on the masses involved.
Investigate and evaluate the design to show fields act between objects that are not touching.
Graph data to describe how kinetic energy relates to mass and speed.
Model how stored potential energy changes when objects interacting at a distance change arrangement.
Design, build and test a device that minimizes or maximizes heat transfer.
Plan an investigation on how energy transferred, type of matter, mass and temperature change are related.
Argue that when an object's kinetic energy changes, energy is transferred to or from it.

units.title: MS-PS4 Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

topics.title: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

outcomes.text: Use math to show how a wave's amplitude relates to its energy.
Model how waves are reflected, absorbed or transmitted by different materials.
Support the claim that digital signals carry information more reliably than analog ones.

units.title: MS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Investigate to show living things are made of one or many cells of different types.
Model how a cell works as a whole and how its parts contribute.
Argue that the body is a system of interacting subsystems made of groups of cells.
Argue how animal behaviors and plant structures affect the chance of successful reproduction.
Explain how environment and genes together influence growth.
Explain the role of photosynthesis in cycling matter and moving energy into and out of organisms.
Model how food is rearranged by chemical reactions into new molecules for growth or energy release.
Explain that sensory receptors send messages to the brain for immediate action or memory.

units.title: MS-LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics

outcomes.text: Analyze data on how resource availability affects organisms and populations.
Explain and predict patterns of interaction among organisms across ecosystems.
Model the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
Argue with evidence that changes to an ecosystem's parts affect its populations.
Evaluate competing designs for keeping biodiversity and ecosystem services.

units.title: MS-LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

topics.title: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

outcomes.text: Model how gene changes on chromosomes can alter proteins with harmful, helpful or neutral effects.
Model why asexual reproduction gives identical offspring and sexual reproduction gives variation.

units.title: MS-LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity

outcomes.text: Analyze fossil patterns showing life's existence, diversity, extinction and change over time.
Explain body similarities and differences among living and fossil organisms to infer relationships.
Compare embryo development across species to find relationships not seen in adult bodies.
Explain how trait variation helps some individuals survive and reproduce in an environment.
Gather information on technologies that change how humans influence inherited traits.
Use math to show how natural selection raises or lowers traits in a population.

units.title: MS-ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe

outcomes.text: Model the Earth-sun-moon system to explain moon phases, eclipses and seasons.
Model how gravity shapes motion in galaxies and the solar system.
Analyze data to find scale properties of solar system objects.
Use rock strata and fossils to explain how the geologic time scale organizes Earth's history.
Model the cycling of Earth's materials and the energy flow that drives it.
Explain how geoscience processes change Earth's surface at different time and size scales.
Analyze fossil, rock, continent-shape and seafloor data as evidence of past plate motion.
Model how the sun's energy and gravity drive water through Earth's systems.
Collect data showing how moving air masses change weather.
Model how uneven heating and Earth's rotation drive air and ocean circulation and regional climates.
Explain how geoscience processes distribute minerals, energy and groundwater unevenly.
Analyze hazard data to forecast events and guide technologies that reduce harm.
Design a method to monitor and reduce a human impact on the environment.
Argue how more people and higher resource use affect Earth's systems.
Ask questions to clarify the factors behind rising global temperatures over the last century.
Define a design problem's criteria and constraints precisely, considering science, people and environment.
Evaluate competing designs with a systematic process against criteria and constraints.
Analyze test data to combine the best features of several designs into a better one.
Build a model that generates data for repeated testing and improving a design.
Use the periodic table and outer-shell electron patterns to predict element properties.
Explain a simple reaction's outcome from outer electrons and periodic trends.
Investigate bulk properties of substances to infer the strength of electrical forces between particles.
Model how energy released or absorbed in a reaction depends on total bond energy change.
Explain how temperature and concentration change a reaction's rate.
Refine a chemical system by changing conditions to increase products at equilibrium.
Use math to show atoms and mass are conserved in a reaction.
Model changes in the nucleus and energy released in fission, fusion and radioactive decay.

units.title: HS-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

topics.title: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

outcomes.text: Analyze data showing how net force, mass and acceleration are related.
Use math to show total momentum is conserved when no net force acts on a system.
Design and refine a device that reduces the force on an object during a collision.
Use Newton's gravitation law and Coulomb's law to predict gravitational and electric forces.
Investigate how current makes a magnetic field and a changing field makes current.
Explain why molecular-level structure matters for how designed materials work.
Build a computational model of one component's energy change from the other's and the energy flows.
Show energy at everyday scale as motion plus position energy of particles or objects.
Design and refine a device that converts energy within given constraints.
Investigate how heat moves between objects of different temperature toward even distribution.
Model two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields, including forces and energy changes.

units.title: HS-PS4 Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

topics.title: Waves and their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

outcomes.text: Use math on frequency, wavelength and speed of waves in different media.
Evaluate questions about the benefits of digital transmission and storage.

subtopics.title: Wave and particle models of light

outcomes.text: Evaluate evidence that electromagnetic radiation fits a wave or a particle model depending on the situation.
Judge claims about how different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation affect matter.
Explain how devices use wave behavior and its interaction with matter to send and capture information and energy.

units.title: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

topics.title: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

outcomes.text: Explain how DNA structure determines protein structure and so the functions of specialized cells.
Model the layered organization of interacting systems in multicellular organisms.
Investigate how feedback mechanisms keep conditions stable.
Model how cell division and differentiation build and maintain complex organisms.
Model how photosynthesis turns light energy into stored chemical energy.
Explain how sugar's carbon, hydrogen and oxygen combine with other elements into amino acids and large carbon molecules.
Model respiration as breaking bonds in food and oxygen and forming new bonds, with a net energy transfer.

units.title: HS-LS2 Ecosystems: Interactions, Energy, and Dynamics

outcomes.text: Use math or computation to explain what affects ecosystem carrying capacity.
Use math to explain factors affecting biodiversity and populations at different scales.
Explain the cycling of matter and flow of energy with and without oxygen.
Use math to support claims about matter cycling and energy flow among organisms.
Model how photosynthesis and respiration cycle carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere and geosphere.
Evaluate claims that ecosystem interactions keep numbers stable but changing conditions can create a new ecosystem.
Design and refine a way to lessen human harm to the environment and biodiversity.
Evaluate evidence for how group behavior affects survival and reproduction.

units.title: HS-LS3 Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

topics.title: Heredity: Inheritance and Variation of Traits

outcomes.text: Ask questions on how DNA and chromosomes code traits passed from parents to offspring.
Defend a claim that inherited variation arises from meiosis, replication errors or environmental mutations.
Use statistics and probability to explain variation and distribution of traits in a population.

units.title: HS-LS4 Biological Evolution: Unity and Diversity

outcomes.text: Explain that common ancestry and evolution are supported by multiple lines of evidence.
Explain that evolution results mainly from population growth, heritable variation, competition and differential survival.
Use statistics and probability to show advantageous heritable traits become more common.
Explain with evidence how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
Evaluate evidence that environmental change can increase some species, create new ones and cause extinctions.
Create or revise a simulation testing a solution to reduce human harm to biodiversity.

units.title: HS-ESS1 Earth's Place in the Universe

outcomes.text: Model the sun's life span and how fusion in its core releases energy that reaches Earth.
Explain the Big Bang using light spectra, galaxy motion and the universe's makeup.
Explain how stars produce elements over their life cycle.
Use math or computation to predict how objects orbit in the solar system.
Evaluate evidence of crust movement and plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.
Use ancient Earth materials, meteorites and planetary surfaces to describe Earth's formation and early history.
Model how internal and surface processes at different scales form continental and ocean-floor features.
Analyze data to show one surface change can cause feedbacks changing other Earth systems.
Model Earth's interior and the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
Use a model to describe how changes in energy flow into and out of Earth's systems change climate.
Investigate the properties of water and how they affect Earth materials and surface processes.
Build a quantitative model of carbon cycling among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere and biosphere.
Argue with evidence that Earth's systems and life evolved together.
Explain how resources, natural hazards and climate change have influenced human activity.
Evaluate competing designs for managing energy and mineral resources by cost and benefit.
Simulate how resource management, human population sustainability and biodiversity relate.
Evaluate or refine a technology that lessens human impacts on natural systems.
Analyze geoscience data and climate models to forecast climate change and its impacts.
Use a computational representation to show how human activity changes relationships among Earth systems.
Analyze a major global challenge to set criteria and constraints reflecting societal needs.
Design a solution to a complex problem by splitting it into smaller solvable problems.
Evaluate a solution against prioritized criteria and trade-offs such as cost, safety, reliability and social impact.
Use a computer simulation to model how proposed solutions affect interacting systems.
